members.name: persuasion_strategy_v5b
members.instructions: This is a chat in which a persuader tries to convince a persuadee to donate part of their task payment to the charity Save the Children. Tag ONLY the final persuader message (the one marked 'Persuader message to tag') with the persuasion strategy or dialogue act it performs. Use the earlier chat only as context for what the message is responding to. If the message does several things, choose its main act; a message that gives information and then adds a short follow-up question is tagged by the information it gives.

criteria.greeting: Opening salutation or pleasantry: hello/hi, asking how the partner is doing, or the persuader answering the partner's question about how they are, however briefly (saying they are fine, well, okay).
criteria.farewell: Closing pleasantry with no thanks in it: wishing a good day or night, goodbye, nice chatting.
criteria.thank: The persuader thanks or expresses appreciation to the persuadee (for donating, their time, the chat), possibly with a farewell attached.
criteria.proposition: Directly asks or urges the persuadee to donate to this charity, asks whether they would consider or be willing to donate (no specific amount asked), or tells the persuadee that the children need them or their help. A plain request; when the urging is backed by an argument or a cost comparison, it is a logical appeal.
criteria.ask_more: After the persuadee has offered or refused, asks them to give more, raise their amount, or reconsider.
criteria.ask_amount: Asks how much the persuadee would like / is willing to donate.
criteria.confirm_amount: Checks or confirms the specific amount the persuadee said they will donate.
criteria.donation_info: Gives practical facts about how this donation works: it comes out of the task payment, the allowed range or that they may give whatever amount they like, the research team forwards it, when or where to enter it, payment methods; also answers to questions about the procedure.
criteria.source_inquiry: Asks whether the persuadee has heard of, knows, or is familiar with Save the Children / the organization.
criteria.personal_inquiry: Asks about the persuadee's own life and involvement: whether they have children, where they are from, whether they donate or volunteer or have done so before, which charities they support, whether they are interested in joining or getting involved in charity work in general.
criteria.task_inquiry: Any other question to the persuadee: their opinion or feelings about charity, the cause or the organization, whether they agree, whether they have questions or want more information, what they say or think.
criteria.credibility: Establishes the organization's trustworthiness or describes what it is and does: its mission, programs, countries served, history, founders, reputation, ratings, share of funds going to programs, pointing to its website, jobs or opportunities it offers, the persuader's role in it; includes statements that the charity is acting on a crisis and answers to questions about the charity.
criteria.emotion: Tries to stir sympathy, sadness or guilt: facts or statistics about children's suffering, death, war, hunger or poverty; asking the persuadee to imagine it; stories about a particular child in need or helped; the persuader expressing sadness about it; also cost or affordability remarks that are framed by sadness or guilt, or that evoke a suffering or starving child.
criteria.logical: Reasons why donating makes sense: the donation will have a real, tangible impact; children need help and donations provide it; plain impersonal assertions that there is need or that help is needed; moral reasoning that we should all help; comparing the small cost to the large benefit, including urging the persuadee to give up a small everyday purchase so the money goes to the children. Phrased neutrally, without sadness, guilt or images of suffering children.
criteria.foot_in_door: Stresses that even a small amount is worthwhile, or asks for just a small amount: even a tiny donation helps, every little bit counts, would they give only a dollar or a few cents.
criteria.self_modeling: The persuader talks about their own giving: their intention to donate now, offering to match the persuadee, or their habit or history of donating.
criteria.personal_story: The persuader narrates their own life experience related to need or charity, other than simply stating that they donate (what they themselves saw, did or went through). Sad stories about other people's children are emotion appeals instead.
criteria.praise: Compliments the persuadee (kind, generous, a good person) or reacts with enthusiasm right after the persuadee commits to donating.
criteria.acknowledge: Reaction to the persuadee's point that carries content: agreeing with their opinion, saying they understand them, glad to hear what they said, sympathizing with them.
criteria.filler: A flat filler with no content: ok, yeah, fine, sure, yes indeed.
criteria.self_answer: A bare answer or remark about the persuader themself that adds nothing: a yes/no reply to a question about the persuader, or saying they share the persuadee's situation or feeling (same for me) without reacting to the persuadee's point. Not replies about how the persuader is doing (greeting).
criteria.off_task: Talk unrelated to the charity or donation: hometowns, weather, hobbies, celebrities, the HIT or task mechanics, jokes.
criteria.other: Anything else: the persuader voicing their own feelings or how hard a decision is without making an appeal, clarifications, typos, incomplete fragments, hostile remarks, statements about what the persuader will talk about.

members.name: variant_b
members.instructions: Below is a conversation where a persuader asks a persuadee to give some of their task earnings to Save the Children. Classify only the last line, the persuader message to tag, by the dialogue act or persuasion strategy it uses. Earlier turns are context only. When the message does more than one thing, pick the act that dominates; information followed by a brief follow-up question counts as the information.

criteria.greeting: Hello/hi at the start of the chat, asking how the other person is, or the persuader saying how they themselves are doing in reply (fine, good, okay), even in a few words.
criteria.farewell: Saying goodbye or wishing the partner a good day/night at the end, without thanking them.
criteria.thank: Expressing thanks or appreciation to the persuadee, for a donation, their time or the conversation, with or without a goodbye.
criteria.proposition: A request that the persuadee donate to this charity, or a question whether they would be willing to (without asking an amount), or telling them the children need them or their help. Only a bare request: urging supported by reasons or a cost comparison is a logical appeal.
criteria.ask_more: Once the persuadee has named an amount or declined, pushing them to give more or to change their mind.
criteria.ask_amount: A question about how much the persuadee wants or is willing to give.
criteria.confirm_amount: Double-checking the amount the persuadee has said they will give.
criteria.donation_info: Practical details of the donation in this task: taken from the task payment, what range is allowed or that any amount is fine, the researchers pass it on, when or where to enter it, how to pay; also replies to procedural questions.
criteria.source_inquiry: A question whether the persuadee knows of, has heard about, or is familiar with Save the Children.
criteria.personal_inquiry: A question about the persuadee's own life and charitable involvement: kids, where they live, whether they give or volunteer or did before, which charities they back, whether they would like to get involved in charity work generally.
criteria.task_inquiry: Any other question put to the persuadee: what they think or feel about charity, the cause or the organization, whether they agree, whether they want more information or have questions.
criteria.credibility: Builds trust in the organization or explains what it is and does: mission, programs, where it works, history, founders, reputation, ratings, how much money reaches programs, its website, roles or opportunities in it including the persuader's; covers the charity responding to a crisis and replies to questions about the charity.
criteria.emotion: Appeals to feelings such as pity, sadness or guilt: facts or numbers about children suffering, dying, at war, hungry or poor; inviting the persuadee to picture it; stories of a specific child in need or helped; the persuader saying it saddens them; cost or affordability remarks wrapped in sadness or guilt or invoking a starving or suffering child.
criteria.logical: Gives reasons that donating is sensible: a donation has concrete impact; children need help and donations supply it; neutral statements that need exists; moral arguments that everyone should help; small cost versus large benefit, such as giving up a minor daily purchase for the children. Neutral in tone, without sadness, guilt or pictures of suffering.
criteria.foot_in_door: Emphasizes that a small gift is worth it, or asks for only a little: any tiny amount helps, every bit counts, just a dollar or a few cents.
criteria.self_modeling: The persuader describes their own giving: that they will donate, that they will match the persuadee, or that they donate regularly or have donated.
criteria.personal_story: A narrative of the persuader's own experience with need or charity, beyond just saying they donate: something they personally saw, did or lived through. Sad accounts about other people's children are emotion appeals.
criteria.praise: Complimenting the persuadee as kind, generous or good, or an enthusiastic reaction just after they commit to give.
criteria.acknowledge: A contentful response to the persuadee's point: agreeing with their view, saying they understand, being glad about what they said, sympathizing.
criteria.filler: A content-free filler: okay, yeah, fine, sure, yes indeed.
criteria.self_answer: A bare remark or yes/no about the persuader themself that adds nothing, or saying they are in the same situation or feel the same, without engaging the persuadee's point. Replies about how the persuader is doing are greetings instead.
criteria.off_task: Chat unrelated to the charity or donation: where people live, weather, hobbies, celebrities, the HIT or task itself, jokes.
criteria.other: Anything else: the persuader airing their own feelings or how hard a choice is without an appeal, clarifications, typo fixes, fragments, hostile remarks, announcing what they will talk about.
